This record is the public front page and bulk-preservation lane for an ongoing open project to produce modern, inspectable LaTeX editions and translation drafts of older mathematics and physics manuscripts. The durable reader files and large provenance files live on Zenodo; the GitHub mirror is used for coordination, issue reports, pull requests, current manifests, and lightweight source snapshots where practical.

How to read this archive. The project is not one uniform pile of OCR and it is not a set of certified critical editions. OCR converted to TeX, formula OCR, crops, and locator files are witness layers for checking and repair. The main scholarly value is in organized reader PDFs, TeX sources, source witnesses, repair ledgers, and translation drafts that can be checked and improved. File counts, upload size, and old progress-bar style labels are not completion metrics and do not imply source certification.

Open these first: best current reader/translation surfaces. The strongest public reader lanes are currently Noether, Weber, Frobenius, Kneser, Sylvester, and al-Battani. These records have coherent reader surfaces or work-level editions for declared scopes, but they remain working drafts rather than certified critical editions.

Serious source-aware work, caveat-heavy. SGA contains real SGA5 page-local repair work and substantial SGA6/SGA7 working translation/source-audit material. It is not OCR-only, but it is also not complete or globally source-faithful. SGA5 is controlled by its page-local workpass cursor; the latest compact promoted SGA5 delta remains p260-p265, while later local French workpass/provenance now reaches p480 in CERT_LOG.md and locally claims body-text completion for the selected 10-exposé SGA5 branch. That later evidence now reports about 60 numbered TeX-fix events (TALLY 59 fixes / max fix #60), ERRATA 115, D001-D193 diagram tracking, and a 306pp/0err compile gate, but recert spot-checks still found real defects and it remains live ledger/provenance until compactly packaged and independently checked. Agent/diagram-aid ledgers are finders rather than certification. SGA5 is not English-synchronized, index-audited, globally source-faithful, independently certified, or critical. SGA6 and SGA7 carry compression and source-check caveats; a July 2026 SGA6 local workpass now explicitly treats the earlier repair033 TeX as a scaffold with paraphrased/condensed regions and mirrors a source-rescribe through entry #182, idx185 / volume p172 / Exposé II p13. Deligne, Bianchi, Gordan, Steinitz, Maxwell, Gibbs, Ukrainian applied mathematics, and the non-European/multilingual mathematics records also contain substantial work, but status varies by paper, page range, table, and diagram. Weber has useful local Phase 2 German workpass evidence, and the active Volume I p1-p99 source gap-pass now reaches p76 (next p77) with §22 complete and about 75-76 numbered fix events recorded; a compact GitHub evidence mirror now lives at sources/weber/weber-vol1-b139-p001-p076-gap-pass-20260703/. The separate completed 20-page Volume I sample-cert audit failed as certification: §26/p90 and §164/p544 require full re-transcription, p400 and p580 content drops were fixed locally, 12 sample pages were clean, and §141-188 should be reverified page-by-page. This is local source-audit/workpass evidence, not whole-volume certification or English synchronization.

Partial streams and mixed shelves. Dedekind, Dirichlet, Gauss, Riemann, and Poincare have useful author records, but should be read package by package rather than as seamless author-complete editions. The classical algebra/arithmetic shelf and additional author cluster are staging/backstop shelves, not blanket quality claims.

OCR/support/provenance or currently unsafe draft lanes. EGA is a French-originals, OCR/support, upstream/community TeX, and partial English draft lane. It is useful for preservation and continuation, but not comparable to SGA's active source-audit workpass lane. Cayley is currently de-promoted: broad PDFs, TeX, unit indexes, and ZIPs are retained for salvage and future repair, but no Cayley range is currently promoted as source-faithful.

Noether local source-control/support head. The Noether author record now fronts R794 as the newest inspected narrow source-control head. R794 integrates one P15 p149 formula equality repair and P30 pp.30-32 emphasis/product-dot restorations over R793, and compiles to a 466-page German cumulative. Because the Noether record is at the 100-file ceiling, R794 should be folded into a curated rollup rather than uploaded loose. This remains source-control/support material only, not a reader release, Noether closure, whole-corpus certification, 650+ source certification, multilingual synchronization, or a critical edition.

Infrastructure. This record, under concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20393488, remains the bulk/raw/provenance landing page so author records do not need to re-upload multi-gigabyte raw archives every time. The workflow and replication packet documents the AI-run scan/OCR/source-witness/TeX/translation/audit/GitHub/Zenodo workflow and its current failure modes. A dedicated interlanguage/methodology lane now preserves Ukrainian/Russian/Interslavic, constructed-language, and terminology-governance apparatus; it is linguistics/methodology material, not a Noether reader release, native-speaker approval, term approval, mathematical source certification, language synchronization proof, or critical edition. A dedicated Lean/formalization sidecar lane now preserves useful Lean 4/mathlib-style candidate material for Noether, Steinitz, Weber, and Jordan; it is not source-fidelity certification, translation certification, page-completeness certification, or a critical edition.

Quality note. This landing page is not a critical edition, and no public record in this project should be read as a critical edition, critically complete edition, or mathematically certified edition unless a future record explicitly says that such certification has been completed. Words such as complete, source-checked, strict, or critical in older filenames may be inherited package labels or structural coverage labels. Verify citation-critical formulas, diagrams, tables, theorem statements, cross-references, and unusual notation against the source scans.

Corrections and contributions. Source comparisons, LaTeX fixes, translation corrections, and reader-facing issue reports can be suggested through the GitHub mirror via issues or pull requests: https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/modern-latex-manuscripts.
